relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: David begins with consultation among military and political leaders.
The whole dispersed community, including priests and Levites, is invited into a national gathering.
The ark becomes a symbol of recovering what Saul's reign neglected.
Public agreement makes the plan popular, not automatically safe.
A vast territory is summoned into one procession.
The ark is approached as the named seat of sacred presence.
A new cart carries the ark while Uzzah and Ahio manage the dangerous movement.
Music and collective force surround a transport system that has not been made safe.
When the oxen stumble, Uzzah reaches to prevent disaster.
The emergency helper dies in a sacred breach the text does not make ethically easy.
David becomes angry and names the place after the rupture.
Celebration collapses into fear and uncertainty.
The ark is redirected into Obed-edom's household rather than David's city.
The household lives with the ark for three months and experiences blessing rather than another death.

contemplative_note: Good intentions, unanimous approval, beautiful music, and sacred purpose do not replace competent planning. Uzzah's body exposes the cost when leaders spiritualize a system failure. Reverence worthy of the Divine must include safety, consent, accountability, and care for the people and animals carrying the holy thing.
